ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #14 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Adjectives: Which is correct? (1 mark)
   A. This is more beautifuler than that.
   B. This is more beautiful than that.
   C. This is beautifullest than that.
   D. This is beautifuller than that.

2. Which is the comparative form of 'little' (amount)? (1 mark)
   A. littler
   B. less
   C. more little
   D. least

3. To compose an email means to (1 mark)
   A. print a message
   B. write a new message
   C. answer a phone
   D. delete a message

4. Where do you see a reply to your email? (1 mark)
   A. In the outbox
   B. In the inbox
   C. In the keyboard
   D. On the wall

5. Dialogues: Which question is inferential? (1 mark)
   A. Which button did they click?
   B. Who wrote the address?
   C. How do you think Baraka felt at the end?
   D. Where do they see the reply?

6. Which noun is uncountable? (1 mark)
   A. milk
   B. egg
   C. chair
   D. pupil

7. Quantifiers: Which is correct? (1 mark)
   A. How many book are there?
   B. How much books are there?
   C. How many books are there?
   D. How much book are there?

8. Where can you find pictures for a composition? (1 mark)
   A. Only on a calendar
   B. Only on money
   C. Books, magazines and websites with a teacher's help
   D. Only in a dictionary

9. A good title for a story about a boy who emails his grandmother is (1 mark)
   A. A Message for Grandmother
   B. The Weather in April
   C. How to Bake Bread
   D. A Trip to the Farm

10. In the story 'The Boy and the Borrowed Phone', what did Otieno do with the strange message? (1 mark)
   A. He showed it to his aunt
   B. He replied at once
   C. He sent it to his class
   D. He typed his school name

11. Which sentence uses the past progressive correctly? (1 mark)
   A. I walking to school when it started to rain.
   B. I was walking to school when it started to rain.
   C. I am walking to school when it started to rain.
   D. I was walk to school when it started to rain.

12. What is the job of a full stop? (1 mark)
   A. To show a question
   B. To show a list
   C. To end a statement or a command
   D. To show strong feeling

13. Which word begins with /w/? (1 mark)
   A. water
   B. very
   C. vet
   D. van

14. What does 'indigenous' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Very expensive
   B. Grown in a factory
   C. Damaged by pests
   D. Belonging naturally to a place

15. Which sentence uses 'its' correctly to show belonging? (1 mark)
   A. Its a fine day.
   B. I think its a goat.
   C. The cow licked its calf.
   D. Its raining today.

16. What is the contraction of 'do not'? (1 mark)
   A. do'nt
   B. don't
   C. d'not
   D. dont

17. How long should the narrative composition be at this level? (1 mark)
   A. About 500 words
   B. About 60 to 80 words
   C. About 10 words
   D. About 300 words

18. In which word is 'gh' silent? (1 mark)
   A. enough
   B. night
   C. tough
   D. cough

19. In which word does the letter s say /z/? (1 mark)
   A. sun
   B. class
   C. easy
   D. sit

20. Which is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Mama may, I go to the shop?
   B. Mama, may I go to the shop?
   C. Mama may I go to the shop.
   D. Mama, may I go to the shop.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. List three places where we use a capital letter. (3 marks)

22. Write two words in which 'gh' is silent and two in which it says /f/. (4 marks)

23. Explain the difference between 'it's' and 'its' with one sentence for each. (4 marks)

24. Punctuate: 'we planted maize beans and sorghum' (2 marks)

25. Write three sentences about your family or school: one comparative, one superlative and one with two adjectives in the right order. (3 marks)

26. Rewrite in the past tense: 'Baraka types a message and clicks Send.' (2 marks)

27. Give three safety rules for using the internet. (4 marks)

28. Explain why we do not say 'I am knowing the answer'. Give the correct sentence. (3 marks)

29. List two facts from the story about how HIV cannot spread. (2 marks)

30. Why did the teacher say the prize message might be a trick? (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #14 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — This is more beautiful than that.
   Long adjectives use more.

2. B — less
   Little, less, least.

3. B — write a new message
   Compose means to write.

4. B — In the inbox
   Received messages are kept in the inbox.

5. C — How do you think Baraka felt at the end?
   You must work it out from clues.

6. A — milk
   We cannot count milk one by one.

7. C — How many books are there?
   Books are countable and plural.

8. C — Books, magazines and websites with a teacher's help
   There are many safe sources.

9. A — A Message for Grandmother
   It suits the story.

10. A — He showed it to his aunt
   He remembered his teacher's advice and asked an adult.

11. B — I was walking to school when it started to rain.
   Past progressive was + verb-ing, with the simple past for the shorter action.

12. C — To end a statement or a command
   A full stop ends statements and commands.

13. A — water
   'Water' begins with /w/, said with rounded lips.

14. D — Belonging naturally to a place
   Indigenous plants and animals are native to a place.

15. C — The cow licked its calf.
   'Its' without an apostrophe shows belonging.

16. B — don't
   The apostrophe replaces the o in 'not'.

17. B — About 60 to 80 words
   The task is a narrative of 60 to 80 words.

18. B — night
   In 'night' the gh is not pronounced.

19. C — easy
   The s in 'easy' is buzzed, like z.

20. B — Mama, may I go to the shop?
   A comma after the person addressed, and a question mark at the end.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: The first word of a sentence; the word I; names of people; names of places; days and months (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: Silent: night, light, high, daughter (any two). /f/: laugh, cough, enough, rough (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: It's means 'it is' or 'it has': It's raining. Its shows belonging: The dog wagged its tail.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for each correct sentence.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: We planted maize, beans and sorghum.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each comma and capital/full stop.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: My brother is taller than I am. He is the tallest boy in his class. He has a big round bag.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: Baraka typed a message and clicked Send.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each verb.

27. (4 marks)
   Answer: Use it with an adult, keep your password secret, do not give your name or address to strangers, tell an adult if something frightens you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule, up to 4.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: 'Know' is a state verb, not an action in progress, so it is not normally used in the progressive form. The correct sentence is 'I know the answer.'
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for state verb explanation, 1 for the correct sentence, 1 for clear expression.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: It cannot spread by playing, shaking hands, sharing a plate or hugging.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct fact.

30. (3 marks)
   Answer: It promised a prize but asked for personal details, and some people send such messages to steal information.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for prize, 1 mark for details, 1 mark for stealing.
